subject: capybara
pitch:
Category: Animal.
Subject: capybara with a small bird on its head.
Style: whimsical.
reasoning:
I'm planning a compact capybara model roughly 1.2m long and 0.55m tall facing forward, with a skeleton including hips, spine, neck, head, jaw, four legs, and a tail stub, plus a small jointed bird perched on its head, building it using joint, chain, sweep, and part primitives to keep things manageable.

I'm laying out the spine as a curved chain from hips through chest, then building the head with a neck joint, a skull sphere, and a boxy snout using frustum shapes, all parented correctly up the hierarchy.

Continuing with jaw, eyes, ears, and nose details—a lower jaw box, black eye spheres with white glints, flattened ear spheres, and a pink blush sphere on the cheeks for a whimsical touch, keeping shapes simple and reliable rather than using texture decals.

Now I'm planning the legs as short chains built from three points each (hip, knee, ankle) so each chain has two spans plus a tip joint, parenting front legs to an upper spine joint and hind legs to the hip, with tapered sweep radii and box-shaped toes at the feet.

For the tail I'm adding a small sphere stub, and for fur I'm using a countershaded mottled brown palette with a pinkish nose for a whimsical touch. Then I'm adding a small bluebird perched on the head, built from a scaled sphere body, a beak made of two cones for upper and lower jaw, eyes, flattened sphere wings, a box tail, and thin rod feet, all parented through a bird joint hierarchy.

I'm positioning the bird's rest pose with wings slightly extended outward, sizing its body sphere, and working out the exact heights so its feet sit flush on the head's skull top while the character's own feet rest at floor level. I'm also considering a tiny flower accent on the bird for extra whimsy.

I'm adding a small decorative daisy near the head, building it from a center sphere plus six petal spheres arranged in a ring using flattened scaled shapes positioned with simple trig around the center point, oriented to lie flat facing upward.

For the eyes, I'm keeping things simple: dark spheres for the eye base plus a small outward-facing textured plane offset along a direction vector to add a glossy highlight look, skipping precise texture detail and just using basic circle/highlight imagery.

Now I'm setting up a helper function to place body parts with position, scale, and rotation, then building the spine as a chain of bones running from the hips joint, which I'll sweep into a barrel-shaped body using an elliptical radius function that varies along the length so the torso bulges naturally and sits above the legs without clipping.

For the head, I'm chaining neck and head joints off the spine's tip, aiming them forward and slightly upward, then adding a jaw joint and lower jaw box underneath the head with a dark line for the mouth.

Now setting up the bone roles (neck, head, jaw), finalizing colors with darker feet and thicker hind legs, then writing out the full export.
